topic: Ambedkar & the Making of the Constitution

items.question: Assess B.R. Ambedkar's contribution as a social reformer and champion of the Depressed Classes in pre-independence India.
items.modelAnswer:
Dr. **B.R. Ambedkar** (1891–1956) transformed the struggle against untouchability from a plea for charity into a demand for **rights, dignity and political power**. Himself born into a **Mahar** family, he armed himself with degrees from **Columbia, the LSE and Gray's Inn** and turned his learning into a sustained assault on caste.

**Direct action:** The **Mahad Satyagraha (1927)** asserted the right of the Depressed Classes to drink from the public **Chavdar tank**, and the symbolic **burning of the Manusmriti** rejected the scriptural sanction for caste. The **Kalaram Temple Entry movement (Nashik, 1930)** extended the fight to sacred space.

**Institution-building:** He mobilised opinion through journals such as **Mooknayak (1920)** and **Bahishkrit Bharat**, and organisations like the **Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha (1924)**, the **Independent Labour Party (1936)** and the **Scheduled Castes Federation (1942)**.

**Constitutional advocacy:** At the **Round Table Conferences** he secured **separate electorates** (Communal Award, 1932); the **Poona Pact (1932)** with Gandhi converted these into **reserved seats**, embedding Depressed-Class representation in the polity. His tract **Annihilation of Caste (1936)** argued that caste could not be reformed, only abolished.

**AP resonance:** His method inspired non-Brahmin and self-respect currents in the Telugu country, complementing leaders like the Andhra Mahila Sabha's **Durgabai Deshmukh**. In sum, Ambedkar fused agitation, organisation and constitutionalism, laying the groundwork for the social-justice guarantees he would later help draft.
keyPoints: Born Mahar (1891); educated at Columbia, LSE, Gray's Inn — turned learning into anti-caste action.
Mahad Satyagraha (1927): Chavdar tank + burning of the Manusmriti; Kalaram Temple Entry (1930).
Built journals (Mooknayak) and bodies (Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha, ILP, SCF).
Won separate electorates (Communal Award 1932); Poona Pact converted them to reserved seats.
Annihilation of Caste (1936): caste must be abolished, not reformed.
AP angle: influenced Telugu non-Brahmin/self-respect currents; contemporary of Durgabai Deshmukh.

items.question: Trace the making of the Indian Constitution by the Constituent Assembly and evaluate Ambedkar's role as Chairman of the Drafting Committee.
items.modelAnswer:
The demand for an Indian-made constitution matured over a decade: first voiced by **M.N. Roy (1934)**, adopted by the **INC (1935)**, conceded in the **August Offer (1940)** and the **Cripps Mission (1942)**, and finally realised under the **Cabinet Mission Plan (1946)**.

**Working of the Assembly:** Elected in **July 1946**, the Assembly first met on **9 December 1946** under **Sachchidananda Sinha**, with **Rajendra Prasad** soon elected permanent President and **B.N. Rau** as Constitutional Advisor. **Nehru's Objectives Resolution (13 Dec 1946, adopted 22 Jan 1947)** set its ideals. Work proceeded through **8 major committees** — Union committees under **Nehru**, States/Advisory under **Patel** — over **11 sessions**. Originally **389 seats**, the Assembly shrank to **299** after partition.

**Ambedkar's role:** The **Drafting Committee**, formed on **29 August 1947** with seven members, was chaired by **Ambedkar**. He piloted the draft through clause-by-clause debate, defended the balance between a **strong Union and federal features**, and articulated the philosophy of **constitutional morality** and safeguards for the weaker sections. His mastery earned him the epithet **'Father of the Indian Constitution'**. The document was **adopted on 26 November 1949** and **came into force on 26 January 1950**, taking about **2 years, 11 months and 18 days**.

**AP angle:** Telugu members shaped the text too — the jurist **Alladi Krishnaswamy Ayyar** sat on the Drafting Committee, while **Durgabai Deshmukh** and **T. Prakasam** contributed to the debates. Ambedkar's stewardship, resting on this collective effort, gave India a durable framework for democracy and social justice.
keyPoints: Idea (M.N. Roy 1934) → INC 1935 → August Offer 1940 → Cripps 1942 → Cabinet Mission 1946.
First meeting 9 Dec 1946 (Sinha); Rajendra Prasad permanent President; Objectives Resolution by Nehru.
8 major committees, 11 sessions; strength 389 → 299 after partition.
Drafting Committee (29 Aug 1947, 7 members) chaired by Ambedkar — 'Father of the Constitution'.
Adopted 26 Nov 1949; enforced 26 Jan 1950; took c. 2 years 11 months 18 days.
AP angle: Alladi Krishnaswamy Ayyar on Drafting Committee; Durgabai Deshmukh & T. Prakasam in debates.
